messages:
Marta: Hey team — customer's dedicated pool `cust-42` started showing a slow queue buildup this morning during the 08:00 traffic ramp. They report rising latencies (p95 from ~120ms -> ~950ms) and intermittent 429s returned by our API. No config changes on their side. Can we triage? :thinking_face:

Sophie: thanks Marta — can you paste a sample response (headers + body) from one of the 429s? also which model variant + request size (tokens) are they using?

Marta: pasted below (scrubbed):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-rate-limit: 100/100
x-rw-rate-window: 60
x-rw-pool-id: cust-42
x-rw-queue-depth: 112
{"error": "rate_exceeded", "message": "throughput cap exceeded"}
```
They're using `gpt-open-compat-16k-q4` with typical prompt+completion ~1200 tokens. Traffic pattern: ramp from 10rps -> 85rps in ~7 minutes, sustained for 30 minutes.

Raj: that x-rw-queue-depth header is useful. Looks like requests are piling at the router before reaching workers. Two hypotheses: (1) reserved-pool allocation hit the hard throughput cap (per-customer token/sec), or (2) worker-side slowdowns (long decode latency for 1.2k tokens) reduced effective throughput.

Raj: quick checks we should run: 1) prom query `sum(rate(rw_server_requests_total{pool=\"cust-42\"}[1m])) by (instance)` to see ingress RPS, 2) `max_over_time(rw_pool_queue_depth{pool=\"cust-42\"}[10m])` to confirm backlog, 3) worker decode p95 `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(rw_decode_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` filtered by pool.

Marta: ran (1) and (2) — ingress shows 82 rps at peak, queue_depth spikes to 120 for ~12 mins. I don't have worker histograms yet.

DeployBot: deploy-notice: config-change applied to `pools/cust-42` at 1728890723 — reserved_capacity reduced from 120rps -> 96rps by autoscaling rollback. Change initiated by rollback-guard job #rollback-2024-06-14T07:45:22Z.

Sophie: oh — DeployBot shows a config change that reduced headroom right before the morning ramp. That explains why a previously-tolerated ramp now overflows the queue. @Raj can you confirm whether the router enforces the throughput cap atomically (dropping) or if we queue then emit 429s when queue > threshold?

Raj: router behavior: we do best-effort queuing up to pool.queue_max (default 100), then we convert to immediate 429s once queue_depth > queue_max + safety_margin. In this case the pool.queue_max for cust-42 is still 100 but the ingress hit 120, so we hit the drop path. Worker slowdowns amplify the effect because effective service rate fell from expected 110rps -> ~80rps due to long-token decodes.

Harry: looping in account — @Marta can we notify customer about a temporary headroom bump? we can increase cust-42 reserved_capacity to 130rps as a short-term mitigation.

Marta: customer agreed to a temporary bump while we investigate.

Raj: proposed remediation plan: 1) immediately bump reserved_capacity to 130rps for cust-42 (hotfix, 2 minute rollout), 2) enable predictive-burst for the pool to allow short bursts beyond reserved but within billing controls, 3) dig into worker decode p95 with model variant to see if quantization/kernel change introduced regressions. Also add an alert for queue_depth > 80 for more than 5m.

Sophie: let's document repro steps so we can validate fix and avoid surprise regressions:
- repro using `wrk` with concurrency 40, request per second target 85, payload ~1200 tokens. Example: 
```
wrk -t10 -c40 -d120s --script=repro.lua https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate
```
Lua script should send the JSON body with `model: gpt-open-compat-16k-q4` and ~1200 input tokens.

Raj: additional repro: run a bursty ramp script (curl loop) to reproduce queue bump and confirm 429s when reserved_capacity lowered. Example:
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate &
sleep 0.2
done
wait
```
This simulates ~5rps per loop iteration concurrently which should reproduce the queue piling.

Marta: I applied the hotfix bump to 130rps (patched via console) at 1728891800. Observed queue_depth drop from 120 -> 8 within 90s and p95 back to ~140ms. Customer confirmed reduced 429s.

Raj: good. Next steps for eng-runtime: 1) analyze decode p95 delta for the model variant between today and last week, 2) check whether the rollback that reduced capacity was expected for cust-42 (why was it targeted), 3) consider increasing default pool.queue_max or making it adaptive based on token length distribution.

Sophie: I'll create a followup ticket with the diag links, alert rule, and customer communication draft. Tagging owners: @Raj for runtime analysis, @Harry for billing/headroom approval for the temporary bump.

DeployBot: incident-log: cust-42 hotfix capacity bump and queue alert added (ticket RW-8391).

Marta: customer ops ACKs, will keep monitoring for 24h. Thanks all :raised_hands:

Sophie: closing the immediate triage. If anything regresses, reopen thread or DM.
